answer: Each agent bonds stake and commits to a polynomial identity, then evaluates it at the epoch point to derive a rate-limit nullifier and proof. Reusing a nullifier in duplicate messages exposes distinct Shamir shares; observers interpolate them to recover the private key, triggering immediate, verifiable collateral slashing. Semaphore proofs conceal membership, while a cipher protects message contents, pigment labels commitment domains, and mirror checks let peers detect equivocation.
